{# GOOD — this file carries no `#jinja2:` header. Its delimiters come from the TASK that
   renders it, which passes `block_start_string: "<%"` and friends
   (`plugins/action/template.py:125-134`). So the grammar of this file is written in another
   file, and reading it needs the link from here back to `templates_chain.yml`. #}
<% if inventory_hostname is defined %>
host = [[ inventory_hostname ]]
<% endif %>

{# NO HINT — with the block delimiters moved by the task, this is ordinary text and the file
   renders it verbatim. Read with the default `{% %}` we would call `notatag` an unknown tag
   and squiggle a template that works. Same trap as the `#jinja2:` header, one file further
   away. #}
{% notatag %}

#jinja2: line_statement_prefix:"#"
{# GOOD in itself — nothing in this file is wrong. It exists to give
   `partials/inherited.j2` an includer whose grammar is not the default one, which is what
   makes that partial unparseable. Measured on ansible-core 2.21.2: rendering this file fails
   with `Encountered unknown tag 'notatag'`, pointing at the partial, so no task renders it.

   Note the comment you are reading is `{# #}` and not `##`: this header sets
   `line_statement_prefix` and NOT `line_comment_prefix`, so a line opening `##` here would be
   a line STATEMENT whose body begins with `#`. That is a syntax error, and it is the mistake
   this fixture was first written with. #}
# include "partials/inherited.j2"

#jinja2: nosuchkey:"x"
{# BAD — `Invalid '#jinja2:' override key 'nosuchkey'.`, measured verbatim on ansible-core
   2.21.2 as `Task failed: Syntax error in template: ...`. One `template-syntax` ERROR, on
   the header line. #}
plain text, and the header above stops the file rendering at all

{# T-040 — one file, three answers. The include target below is a bare name, and the search
   path that resolves it belongs to the *task doing the rendering*, not to this file. Measured
   on ansible-core 2.21.2 with this exact fixture:

       rendered from roles/edge-proxy  ->  roles/edge-proxy/templates/shared.j2
       rendered from roles/edge-cache  ->  roles/edge-cache/templates/shared.j2
       rendered from a play-level task ->  templates/shared.j2

   So "go to definition" on this line has no single answer. It jumps to the play-level
   `templates/shared.j2` — the third row, correct for a play-level render and one of three.
   Offering all three needs the link from this file back to the tasks that render it, which is
   T-015's, so the jump is "a file this include reaches" rather than "the file". #}
{% include "shared.j2" %}

#jinja2: line_statement_prefix:"#", line_comment_prefix:"##"
## GOOD — the sixth and seventh lexer states. A line opening with `#` (blanks allowed before
## it) is a statement; `##` runs to end of line and vanishes. Both are ordinary
## `TemplateOverrides` fields, so this header is all it takes to change the grammar.
## MEASURED THE HARD WAY — this include names `partials/plain.j2` and not
## `partials/header.j2`, which every other template here uses. `header.j2` opens with
## `# rendered for {{ inventory_hostname }}`, and under THIS file's delimiters that leading
## `#` makes it a line statement: ansible fails the render with
## `Encountered unknown tag 'rendered'`. The delimiters belong to the whole render, not to
## the file that declares them, so a partial written for the default grammar can become
## unparseable purely by who includes it.
# include "partials/plain.j2"
# for h in ["alpha", "beta"]
host = {{ h }}   ## this trailing comment is stripped from the output
# endfor

{# GOOD — mixing is legal and measured: a block opened with braces can be closed by a line
   statement. Before the line states existed we read this as an unclosed `{% if %}` and put a
   `template-syntax` ERROR on a template ansible renders fine. #}
{% if true %}
mixed = yes
# endif

## NO HINT — a `#` in the middle of a line is not a statement: the rule is anchored to the
## start of the line, so this next line survives verbatim.
